mentions.name: Offline Home Photo Library Browser
mentions.description: A fully offline, Apple-only, subscription-free home photo library browser. It runs in the background on a Mac (e.g. a Mac Mini), imports photo folders from separate libraries on different Macs, and serves all photos to an iPhone or iPad over the home network with no configuration. Photos are browsed through a filter sidebar organized by date, place, album, people, and event—deliberately not an AI/search-based library—with all filters laid out for exploration. It requires no iCloud, no telemetry, and no subscriptions, avoids lock-in by supporting full export of photo organization in photo metadata, and is not a photo editor or Apple Photos replacement—just a seamless way to browse historical photos at home.
mentions.problem: Photo libraries are split across multiple Apple devices, and accessing them typically means relying on iCloud, telemetry, subscriptions, or accepting lock-in; the app removes the need for cloud services to view and organize your own photos at home.
mentions.audience: Home users with multiple Apple devices who want to browse their own photos without cloud services or subscriptions
mentions.source_excerpt: I'm working on a fully offline, apple only (for now), subscription-free home photo library browser.
